Consult Summary:
- 42-year-old female presents with acute onset shortness of breath for ~1 hour while sitting; recent cough since yesterday and 4 weeks postpartum after Cesarean section; clinician concerned about possible thromboembolic event and advised urgent ED assessment; patient will self-transport with infant.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Sudden onset shortness of breath beginning approximately one hour prior while sitting and watching TV.
- Timeline / progression:
  - Cough began yesterday.
  - Shortness of breath started acutely over the last hour and was noted to be current at time of consult.
  - C-section performed 4 weeks ago.
- Exacerbating / relieving factors:
  - Patient reports becoming more anxious/stressed which is associated with feeling her heart racing.
  - No specific relieving factors reported.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Cough starting yesterday; patient reports not bringing up sputum.
  - Palpitations / feeling heart beating more than normal.
  - Chest feels sore with deep breaths; C-section scar is tender.
  - No chest pain described as focal pain (patient denied typical chest pain).
- Systems review / pertinent negatives (as mentioned):
  - Denies expectoration of sputum.
  - No report of fever, syncope, or focal leg symptoms recorded in the transcript.
  - Baby at home is well; no respiratory illness in baby.
  - No other medical complaints reported during consult.

Past Medical History:
- Recent obstetric history:
  - Cesarean section 4 weeks prior.
  - Postoperative course: required opioids (codeine) for pain; taking "fairly regularly" initially but states she probably has not taken it for ~1 week.
- Other medical history:
  - Patient states "no" other medical problems when asked.
- Allergies:
  - Allergy to ibuprofen; specific reaction not documented.
- Medications:
  - Codeine — dose/route/frequency not documented (used for post-C-section analgesia; discontinued approximately 1 week ago).

Social History:
- Current living/support:
  - Partner at work; patient is alone at home with baby at time of consult.
  - Patient will transport herself and infant to hospital.
- Smoking / alcohol / substance use:
  - Not discussed / not documented.

Family History:
- Mother has history of clots in her legs (history of venous thromboembolism).

Physical Examination:
- Vitals:
  - Radial pulse self-count: patient counted 30 beats during the timed palpation instructed by clinician; clinician interpreted this as "slightly fast" at the time of consult. (Exact heart rate, time interval, and other vital signs not documented.)
- General / focused exam findings:
  - Patient reports feeling anxious/stressed and palpitations.
  - C-section scar tender to palpation (patient-reported).
  - No formal clinician-performed cardiopulmonary or extremity examination documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or available in the transcript.
- No imaging, laboratory tests, pulse oximetry, or ECGs documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute shortness of breath / possible pulmonary embolism (clinician concern)
  - Assessment:
    - Acute-onset dyspnea in a patient 4 weeks postpartum following Cesarean section; clinician concerned about possible thromboembolic event (leg clot or pulmonary embolus) given recent surgery.
  - Plan:
    - Urgent referral to hospital emergency department for further evaluation (patient advised to go promptly).
    - Two transport options offered: call ambulance or self-transport with baby; patient elected to self-transport.
    - Advised to take baby essentials and travel fairly quickly.
    - Advised to withhold codeine prior to hospital evaluation.
    - If clot identified in hospital, clinicians may administer anticoagulation.
- Issue 2: Cough since yesterday (possible alternative/associated cause of dyspnea)
  - Assessment:
    - Cough without sputum present for ~1 day; contribution to dyspnea unclear.
  - Plan:
    - Evaluation in ED as above; further assessment and investigations to determine respiratory infection vs other causes.
- Issue 3: Postoperative pain / recent Cesarean section
  - Assessment:
    - Ongoing postoperative tenderness at C-section scar; recent opioid analgesia use (codeine).
  - Plan:
    - Pain and wound assessment to be performed in ED as appropriate; discontinue codeine until evaluated.
- General plan items:
  - ED evaluation may include vitals, pulse oximetry, ECG, D-dimer/imaging (not documented but implied by clinician discussion), and treatment as indicated.
  - Patient to proceed to hospital promptly with infant; clinician did not arrange ambulance at patient’s request.

Quality checks / document_quality:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Full vital signs (blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature) are not documented.
  - Formal clinician physical examination (cardiovascular, respiratory, abdominal, extremities including leg exam for DVT) not documented.
  - Details of the pulse count time interval and calculated heart rate are not provided.
  - Specifics of ibuprofen allergy reaction are not documented.
  - Codeine dose, route, and frequency are not documented.
  - No laboratory or imaging results available.
  - Lactation status and breastfeeding considerations (medication safety) not documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Transcript is generally clear and audible; clinician and patient statements were intelligible.
